answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of non-memory-hard computational work per identity to act as a resilient timber of the network architecture. Each agent must solve unique puzzles, where the verifier treats every valid output like a spectral plume rising from the compute process to prove expenditure. While an honest node pays this cost for a single identity, an attacker who tries to wander across the protocol to spawn 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, effectively hitting a wall of exhaustion. Fraud triggers an identity burn, and the ledger rejects all duplicate outputs.
